notes:
**Document (134-2.148.note.document).** This continuation sheet has author page number 3 and archive pencil foliation 148. It refers to the correspondent’s observations “p. 5”. No date, salutation, signature or closing appears. The page ends in the uncertain incomplete fragment dévelop/divulg followed by a visible continuation hyphen; no following page supplied a completion.

**Recalled error (134-2.148.claim.former_belief).** The author thanks the correspondent for correcting an “erreur grossière”, attributed to his ignorance of top. algébrique and homotopie. He describes his earlier belief that sufficiently associative and commutative H-espaces, expressed by equivalence to Ω raised to i with i arbitrarily large, corresponded to commutative topological groups. “j’étais en effet dans le sentiment” presents this as the belief being corrected. The transcription records that account; it neither re-proves nor independently refutes the underlying claim.

**Questions and proposed identification (134-2.148.claim.yoga).** “je suis toujours intrigué par la question suivante” introduces the question of an analogue of the tapis de Dold-Puppe for (1/2) simplicial groups, “pas néc. commutatifs”, and “et quelle forme prend-il ?”. The diagram links ens. 1/2 simplicial and ∞-groupoïde with one double-headed arrow. The author calls this an ultimate “set-theoretic” version of Dold-Puppe, describes the abelian groups in (∞-cat) as “ne … sont autres … que” the complexes de chaines in (Ab), and says “Il faudrait donc déterminer” the groups of (∞-cat). He begins to discuss (1-cat) before the page ends. The diagram’s groupoïde and the prose’s ∞-cat are kept as written; no harmonization or theorem verification is implied.

**Mathematics and ink (134-2.148.note.readings).** The possible pre-Ω prime prompted a separate crop inspection: the detached upright exists, but its intended role remains uncertain, while Ω, raised i, baseline i and X are legible. The three readers inspected both fractions, both arrowheads, every infinity occurrence, Ab and (1-cat). The diagram’s singular endings are clear. The overwritten old noun remains tentatively catégorie, with its deletion state definite and its letters uncertain. H acknowledges overwriting in a note but does not recover the older noun; that acknowledgment is not an H doubt mark. The omitted ne, autres and que and the quotation extent were individually confirmed on crops. No mathematical expectation replaced a written symbol or supplied an absent one.

**Other decisions and limits.** Grossière and dû are resolved; dû retains the visible circumflex and lack of final e. Équivalent has no final s, recorded as a possible agreement slip only. The final s of commutatifs remains uncertain. The low mark after t is not at apostrophe height, but may be either a joining hyphen or a detached t cross-stroke. Three isolated possible points are preserved with low confidence, after des, after p. 5., and after n’y; their intended textual role is unresolved. Both quote pairs are raised strokes, and chaines has an i dot without circumflex. The two encodings of the joining stroke in Dold-Puppe are reviewed but excluded as typographic differences. No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate was performed.
